title: A pointed etale span over a smooth base restricts to an etale slice
statement: Let $X\to S$, $Y\to T$, $q:S'\to S$, and $\lambda':S'\to T$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $q$ smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $s'\in S'$, put $s=q(s')$ and $t=\lambda'(s')$, and suppose $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(s')$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-residue-field]. Put $X'=X\times_SS'$ and $Y'=Y\times_{T,\lambda'}S'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $a':H'\to X'$ and $c':H'\to Y'$ be étale $S'$-morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism], with a point $h'\in H'$ over $s'$. Put $x'=a'(h')$ and $y'=c'(h')$, and let $x\in X$ be the image of $x'$. Suppose $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(x')$, $\kappa(x')\to\kappa(h')$, and $\kappa(y')\to\kappa(h')$ are isomorphisms. Then there exist an open neighbourhood $O\subseteq S'$ of $s'$ [def-weil-open-immersion], a closed immersion $i:V\hookrightarrow O$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $v\in V$ mapping to $s'$, such that $V\to S$ is étale, $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(v)$ is an isomorphism, and the underlying fibre over $s$ is $\{v\}$. Put $\tau=\lambda' i:V\to T$, regarding $i$ also as a map to $S'$, and put $W=H'\times_{S'}V$. The fibre of $W\to H'$ over $h'$ is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(h')$, so it has a unique point $w$ with $\kappa(h')\to\kappa(w)$ an isomorphism. The canonical comparison maps identify, compatibly with projections, $W\cong H'\times_{X'}(X\times_SV)$ and $W\cong H'\times_{Y'}(Y\times_{T,\tau}V)$. Consequently the induced maps $W\to X\times_SV$, $W\to Y\times_{T,\tau}V$, and $W\to X$ are étale. They commute over $S$ and $V$, $w$ maps to $x$ and $v$, $\tau(v)=t$, and $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(w)$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: First $s'$ is closed in the fibre $S'_s$. Indeed canonical point naturality [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality] and [def-pc-fibre-product] lift $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s')\to S'$ to the fibre. It is a $\kappa(s)$-rational point by the assumed residue-field isomorphism. If $r$ specializes this point, choose an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $r$ in the fibre; it also contains $s'$. Evaluation $A\to\kappa(s')=\kappa(s)$ is surjective because it is a $\kappa(s)$-algebra map. Its kernel is maximal, so $r=s'$. This uses the subspace identification of the fibre in [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and the prime-ideal description in [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The residue extension is finite separable because it is an isomorphism. Thus [lem-trf-smooth-point-etale-immersion] applies to the smooth map $q$ at $s'$, giving an immersion $V\to S'$, a point $v$ over $s'$, an etale composite $V\to S$, and singleton underlying fibre over $s$. Factor the immersion as a closed immersion $i:V\to O$ followed by an open immersion $O\to S'$, as in [def-weil-closed-immersion]; the image of $O$ contains $s'$.

proof.text: The open and closed immersion residue maps are isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-residue-field-iso]. Hence $\kappa(s')\to\kappa(v)$ is an isomorphism. Composing with $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(s')$ gives the required isomorphism $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(v)$: these are the specified maps, since local stalk maps and their residue-field quotients compose [def-weil-residue-field]. Set $\tau=\lambda' i$ and $W=H'\times_{S'}V$. Naturality of the canonical point morphisms $j_z:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)\to Z$ gives $i j_v=j_{s'}\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(s')\to\kappa(v))$. Its inverse residue isomorphism therefore lifts $j_{s'}$ to $V$. Compose this lift with $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(s')\to\kappa(h'))$ to lift the structural point morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(h')\to S'$ to $V$.

source.place: Tag 0GDX, final paragraph: pointed restriction; point morphism naturality expanded

proof.text: By the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product], the fibre of $W\to H'$ at $h'$ identifies over $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(h')$ with $F=V\times_{S'}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(h')$. The point morphism to $S'$ factors through $O$, so this is also $V\times_O\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(h')$. Base-change stability of closed immersions [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b) makes $F\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(h')$ a closed immersion. The lift from step 2 supplies its section, so $F$ is nonempty. By the affine quotient characterization [def-weil-closed-immersion], $F=\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(h')/I)$ for a proper ideal $I$ of the field $\kappa(h')$; thus $I=0$. This identifies the fibre canonically with $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(h')$. The fibre-point morphism sends its sole point to $w\in W$ over $h'$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Its residue maps give $\kappa(h')\to\kappa(w)\to\kappa(h')$ with composite identity. Field homomorphisms are injective, so the second map is also surjective and both are inverse isomorphisms. Thus the structural map $\kappa(h')\to\kappa(w)$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: For any test scheme $P$, a map $P\to W$ is a pair $(b:P\to H',d:P\to V)$ with equal maps to $S'$. The pair $(a' b,d)$ is exactly a map to $X'\times_{S'}V$ over $X'$; forgetting this forced component is the inverse construction. Also $X'\times_{S'}V\cong X\times_SV$: keep the $X$- and $V$-components, and recover the $S'$-component as $i d$. The same constructions with $c'$ and $Y$ use $\tau=\lambda' i$ and give $Y'\times_{S'}V\cong Y\times_{T,\tau}V$. Uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product] proves that the resulting comparisons are inverse isomorphisms and preserve every indicated projection. This gives precisely the two comparison isomorphisms of the statement.

proof.text: Under the step-4 comparisons, $W\to X\times_SV$ and $W\to Y\times_{T,\tau}V$ are the base changes of $a'$ and $c'$, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. The projection $X\times_SV\to X$ is etale by the same lemma applied to the etale map $V\to S$. Their composite $W\to X$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](2). The projection equalities proved in step 4 give all commutative triangles over $S$ and $V$. At $w$ they give the images $h'$, $x'$, $x$ and $v$, and $\tau(v)=\lambda'(s')=t$. Finally the specified residue map $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(w)$ is the composite of the assumed isomorphisms $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(x')\to\kappa(h')$ and the isomorphism of step 3; composition of local stalk maps verifies that it is the required map [def-weil-residue-field].
